findings.claim: For the quarter ended September 30, 2026, Duke Energy reported total operating revenues of $9.104 billion versus $8.542 billion a year earlier, net income available to common stockholders of $1.551 billion versus $1.407 billion, and basic and diluted EPS of $1.99 versus $1.81.
findings.source_title: Duke Energy Corporation Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: On November 5, 2026 Duke Energy narrowed 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $6.70 to $6.80, said year-to-date performance positions it to deliver near the top of that range, and reaffirmed long-term adjusted EPS growth of 5% to 7% through 2030 off the 2025 guidance midpoint of $6.30, with confidence to earn in the top half beginning in 2028.
findings.source_title: Duke Energy third-quarter 2026 earnings release, Exhibit 99.1

findings.claim: Nine-month 2026 reported EPS was $5.34 and adjusted EPS was $5.35, compared with $4.81 a year earlier, and Electric Utilities and Infrastructure third-quarter segment income was $1,817 million versus $1,658 million.
findings.source_title: Duke Energy third-quarter 2026 earnings release, Exhibit 99.1

findings.claim: Duke Energy said it is executing a generation build to add 16 gigawatts of capacity by 2031.
findings.source_title: Duke Energy third-quarter 2026 earnings release, Exhibit 99.1

findings.claim: Management said data-center development remains a significant contributor to projected load growth and that Duke is expanding data-center electric service agreements that include financial protections so the customers driving the investment bear the related costs.
findings.source_title: Duke Energy Corporation Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: On October 1, 2026 Duke Energy declared a quarterly common dividend of $1.085 per share payable December 16, 2026 to holders of record on November 13, 2026, said it has paid a common dividend for 100 consecutive years, and said its electric utilities serve 8.7 million customers and own 55,700 megawatts.
findings.source_title: Duke Energy announces dividend payments to shareholders, October 1, 2026

findings.claim: At September 30, 2026 long-term debt was $84.332 billion and current maturities of long-term debt were $6.116 billion, compared with $80.108 billion and $7.104 billion at December 31, 2025, and third-quarter interest expense was $967 million versus $902 million.
findings.source_title: Duke Energy Corporation Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: On November 19, 2026 Duke Energy issued $875 million of 6.05% senior notes due 2036, sold to the underwriters at a discount.
findings.source_title: Duke Energy Corporation Form 8-K filed November 19, 2026

findings.claim: In March 2026 Duke Energy executed an equity distribution agreement to sell up to $6 billion of common stock through September 2028, and during the nine months ended September 30, 2026 it priced equity forwards on 6,561,683 shares at initial forward prices from $119.71 to $131.82, with settlement expected by December 31, 2027 and no proceeds recorded until then.
findings.source_title: Duke Energy Corporation Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: The July 17, 2026 Duke Energy Carolinas settlement set a 9.8% ROE and a cumulative retail revenue increase of $496 million, or 7.4%, versus the November 20, 2025 request for $1.0 billion, or 15.0%, and a 10.95% ROE; the August 5, 2026 Duke Energy Progress settlement set the same 9.8% ROE and a cumulative increase of $338 million, or 6.8%, versus a request for $729 million, or 15.1%.
findings.source_title: Duke Energy Corporation Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: On November 16, 2026 the North Carolina Utilities Commission approved the Carolinas and Progress revenue-requirement settlements, including a 9.8% ROE and a 53% equity ratio, historic rate bases of about $25.7 billion and $17.8 billion, and multiyear-plan capital of about $3.8 billion and $3.4 billion; the companies expect revised rates on January 1, 2027 and $10 million of pretax charges at each utility in the fourth quarter, and said they are still assessing the new data-center rate schedule.
findings.source_title: Duke Energy Corporation Form 8-K filed November 17, 2026

findings.claim: For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, Duke Energy Carolinas and Duke Energy Progress recorded $248 million pretax, $189 million after a $59 million tax benefit, for legal settlements, North Carolina rate-case regulatory settlements, and an energy-efficiency regulatory liability.
findings.source_title: Duke Energy third-quarter 2026 earnings release, Exhibit 99.1

findings.claim: On September 24, 2026 the Clermont County Board of Commissioners sued Duke Energy Beckjord, LLC, Duke Energy Ohio, and other owners of the former W.C. Beckjord Station, alleging coal-ash units contributed to groundwater contamination and seeking injunctive relief, civil penalties, and remediation; the complaint does not specify a dollar amount.
findings.source_title: Duke Energy Corporation Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: Duke Energy's Carolina Long Bay offshore-wind lease was canceled effective September 23, 2026 under a Department of the Interior settlement, and the company received the $129 million settlement proceeds in October 2026.
findings.source_title: Duke Energy Corporation Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: Piedmont closed the sale of its Tennessee natural-gas business to Spire on March 31, 2026 for approximately $2.5 billion in cash, and Duke recorded a $368 million pretax gain for the nine months ended September 30, 2026.
findings.source_title: Duke Energy Corporation Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: Piedmont's average number of natural-gas customers in the third quarter of 2026 was 996,464, down 17.0% from 1,200,097 a year earlier, after the March 31, 2026 sale of the Tennessee business.
findings.source_title: Duke Energy third-quarter 2026 earnings release, Exhibit 99.1

findings.claim: Nine-month operating cash flow was $7.889 billion versus $8.672 billion, a $783 million decline driven mainly by a $1.5 billion swing in other assets and liabilities from higher deferred fuel, purchased power, and storm restoration, while capital, investment, and acquisition expenditures were $12.566 billion versus $9.881 billion.
findings.source_title: Duke Energy Corporation Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: On March 3, 2026 an affiliate of Brookfield Super-Core Infrastructure Partners acquired a 9.19% interest in Florida Progress for about $2.8 billion, and the affiliate has indicated an intent to raise its December 2026 investment from $200 million to $1.2 billion and to fund the remaining $2 billion in 2027; third-quarter net income attributable to noncontrolling interests was $85 million versus $33 million.
findings.source_title: Duke Energy Corporation Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: At September 30, 2026 Duke Energy had $451 million of cash and $8.0 billion available under its $10 billion master credit facility, whose termination date was extended in March 2026 to March 2031, and management said it expects sufficient liquidity; the 10-Q does not contain a going-concern warning.
findings.source_title: Duke Energy Corporation Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026

upcoming_catalysts.event: Duke Energy Carolinas and Duke Energy Progress expect to implement the North Carolina rates approved on November 16, 2026.
Duke Energy expects to merge Duke Energy Progress into Duke Energy Carolinas, and lenders consented to that combination in the November 9, 2026 credit-facility amendment.
Quarterly common dividend of $1.085 per share payable to holders of record on November 13, 2026.
Under Indiana House Enrolled Act 1002, Duke Energy Indiana must file its first multiyear rate plan between November 15 and December 15, 2026.

The North Carolina Utilities Commission order on the 2025 Carolinas Resource Plan is expected by December 31, 2026, and the South Carolina commission's order on the 2026 plan is expected by June 2027 after an April 2027 hearing.
Brookfield's affiliate is scheduled to invest at least another $200 million in Florida Progress no later than December 31, 2026, and has indicated an intent to make that closing $1.2 billion.

policy_links.policy: North Carolina Utilities Commission orders approving the Duke Energy Carolinas and Duke Energy Progress performance-based rate settlements
policy_links.bottleneck: commission approval of rate recovery for transmission, distribution, generation, storage, and solar investment
policy_links.revenue_mechanism: The November 16, 2026 orders approve the revenue-requirement settlements, including a 9.8% return on equity, and the companies expect to collect the revised North Carolina retail rates beginning January 1, 2027.

policy_links.policy: Inflation Reduction Act transferable nuclear, solar, and investment tax credits
policy_links.bottleneck: monetizing tax credits and returning their net value to customers
policy_links.revenue_mechanism: In April 2026 Duke Energy Carolinas, Duke Energy Progress, and Duke Energy Florida agreed to sell up to $3.1 billion of net tax credits, with proceeds expected through 2029, and are working with commissions to pass the net realizable value back to customers rather than retain it as revenue.

policy_links.policy: EPA Partial Repeal Rule of Clean Air Act section 111 greenhouse-gas standards for power plants
policy_links.bottleneck: carbon-capture requirements on new and reconstructed gas turbines
policy_links.revenue_mechanism: The September 17, 2026 final rule repeals carbon-capture requirements and retains efficiency-based standards for certain new units; Duke said the rule is generally consistent with the pace of its existing capital plan, which is recovered through regulated rates.

key_risks.risk: Long-term debt of $84.332 billion plus $6.116 billion of current maturities, with third-quarter interest expense of $967 million, while nine-month capital spending of $12.566 billion exceeded operating cash flow of $7.889 billion.
An at-the-market program allows issuance of up to $6 billion of common stock through September 2028, and forwards on 6,561,683 shares were already priced in the first nine months of 2026.

The approved North Carolina settlements cut the requested cumulative revenue increases and the requested ROE from 10.95% to 9.8%, and Duke said it is still assessing the data-center tariff portion of the November 16 orders.
The company warns that results could suffer if electricity use by data centers is lower than currently projected.

Coal-ash compliance remains uncertain: Duke is challenging the 2024 CCR rule, the EPA has proposed rescinding or modifying parts of it and said the impact could be material, and Clermont County has sued over the Beckjord site without stating a damage amount.

dilution_events_last_12m.description: March 2026 at-the-market equity distribution agreement for up to $6 billion of common stock through September 2028. During the nine months ended September 30, 2026, equity forwards were priced on 6,561,683 shares at initial forward prices from $119.71 to $131.82; settlement is expected by December 31, 2027 and no proceeds are recorded until then. Cash issuance of common stock in those nine months was zero.

notes: The November 5 10-Q still described the North Carolina settlements as awaiting a commission order. The November 17 8-K reports that the November 16 orders approved them. Nine-month EPS from continuing operations in the 10-Q EPS footnote is $5.32; reported EPS of $5.34 in the earnings release includes discontinued operations. The master-credit-facility table shows $7,972 million of Duke Energy available capacity, which the MD&A rounds to $8.0 billion. The 17% drop in Piedmont gas customers follows the Tennessee sale, not an organic loss of the remaining franchise. Brookfield's larger December 2026 funding is an indicated intent on top of a contractual $200 million minimum. No going-concern language or delisting notice was found. The $10 million fourth-quarter charges at each Carolina utility had not been recorded as of the November 17 8-K.
